Unreal exposes several programmatic surfaces. Python editor scripting can automate asset tasks, place Actors and control the Editor from custom UIs. The Remote Control API serves HTTP and WebSocket and can call any Blueprint-callable function. C++ source access and the cook/UAT command-line tools cover building and packaging. None of these is documented as giving full parity with the Editor UI: Remote Control is limited to Blueprint-exposed functions, and Python is framed as automating specific workflows rather than mirroring every UI action. Missing for 10: an explicit statement or proof of UI-to-API parity, coverage of UI-only Editor operations, and independent hands-on confirmation that these APIs cover full Editor workflows.

Missing for 10: a documented built-in export of assets and levels to open, standard formats, any statement on project or asset format openness, and hands-on evidence of a successful full-project migration out of Unreal.
